anya: Heads-up — billing team flagged a ~15% jump in per-token cost for /chat-stream after the recent runtime deploy. I pulled profiler samples and token accounting; looks like latency per token went up and billed tokens for some routes diverged from runtime tokens. Can eng-platform + runtime help reconcile?

leo: Do we have kernel-selection logs correlated with the spike window? If we fell back to a slow generic kernel that could increase latency and pushing more timeouts/retries. Quick queries I ran: `sum(rate(kernel_fallbacks_total[5m])) by (model)` and `rate(per_token_latency_ms_sum[5m]) / rate(per_token_latency_ms_count[5m])`

maria: We do. For redwood-7b we saw `kernel_selector_fallbacks{kernel="generic"}` jump at 2025-11-02T03:12:xxZ. Batcher wait time rose too. Pprof shows heavy memory copying path — probably triggered by sequence length distribution change. Attaching small snippet from the pprof: ```# pprof flame graph excerpt
504ms copy_kv_values
210ms attention_kernel_generic
```

ben: Important note: billing pipeline uses `billing.tokens_charged` which is sourced from the API layer. Runtime exposes `runtime.tokens_generated` and `runtime.tokens_consumed`. We need to prove billed == generated (mod discounts/rounding). If kernel fallback causes retries or additional tokens (e.g., safety rewrite), billed could diverge.

sam: We already have customers asking about their invoices. Before we talk credits we need a clear reconciliation process + reproducible queries. Can we create a single dashboard with: billed tokens, runtime tokens_generated, runtime.tokens_consumed, kv_hit_rate, avg_token_latency_ms by route?

iris: I can add dashboard panels. Plan: create a per-route panel showing `sum by(route)(increase(billing.tokens_charged[1h]))` vs `sum by(route)(increase(runtime.tokens_generated[1h]))`, plus `increase(runtime.tokens_consumed[1h])`. Also add `avg_over_time(per_token_latency_ms[1m])` split by `kernel` label and `kv_hit_rate` (kv_hits / kv_lookups).

maria: Also proposing a new metric `kernel_selector_decision{model,kernel,reason}` where reason ∈ {"seq_len","quant_compat","mem_pressure"}. That lets us filter panels to see why selector chose the generic path. I'll add it in the next runtime roll.

leo: Good. Also we need a reconciliation alert: when `abs(billing.tokens_charged - runtime.tokens_consumed) / runtime.tokens_consumed > 0.01` for 5m raise P1. I'll add a monitoring rule.

ben: For the billing team, here's a starter SQL to join events (Postgres) so finance can run ad-hoc checks: ```sql
-- billed vs runtime tokens per route per hour
SELECT hour, route,
  sum(billed_tokens) AS billed,
  sum(runtime_tokens_consumed) AS runtime_consumed
FROM billing_events be
LEFT JOIN runtime_token_summaries rt ON be.request_id = rt.request_id
GROUP BY hour, route
ORDER BY hour DESC
LIMIT 200;
```

iris: Dashboard action list: 1) per-route billed vs runtime tokens (1h,6h,24h), 2) panel: avg_token_latency_ms by kernel+route, 3) panel: kv_hit_rate heatmap by model+route, 4) scatter: kernel_fallbacks vs billed/runtime delta. I'll link when done.

maria: FYI instrumented an extra counter for `batcher.batch_size_histogram` and `batcher.wait_time_ms_bucket` so we can see if batching heuristics changed throughput. Early signal: batch_size median dropped from 16->9 in the window. That could explain higher per-token overhead.

leo: Action items recap: 1) iris add dashboard + panels (ETA today) 2) maria emit `kernel_selector_decision` and batcher hist metrics (next deploy) 3) leo add reconciliation alert & add integration test ensuring billing pipeline uses runtime.tokens_consumed for chargeable tokens 4) ben manage customer comms for invoices (holding credits until we confirm instrumentation) 5) sam to assemble sample invoice reconciliations for impacted accounts.

deploy-bot: deploy: perf-instrumentation -> staging :white_check_mark: (maria, iris)

anya: Thanks — once dashboards are up let's run the reconciliation queries for the week window where spike happened and post results here. If we see >1% unexplained delta I'll open a rollback/credits discussion.

ben: One more snippet for PromQL reconciliation to put on the dashboard: ```promql
-- billed tokens (ingested into prometheus via billing exporter)
sum(increase(billing_tokens_charged_total[1h])) by (route)

-- runtime tokens consumed
sum(increase(runtime_tokens_consumed_total[1h])) by (route)

-- delta pct
(sum(increase(billing_tokens_charged_total[1h])) by (route) - sum(increase(runtime_tokens_consumed_total[1h])) by (route))
/ sum(increase(runtime_tokens_consumed_total[1h])) by (route)
```

iris: Dashboard pushed to Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/AbCdEf/perf-billing-recon (panels: billed vs runtime, kernel latency split, kv heatmap). Posting screenshots in thread.

anya: Verified snapshot for /chat-stream: billed vs runtime delta = 0.9% over 24h (within tolerance) but we see a 7% delta for route /batch-embed where kernel_fallbacks spiked. Next step: run detailed trace sampling for /batch-embed and consider temporary pin of kernel profile or quantized model variant.

maria: I'll schedule trace sampling and add a canary deployment pinning quantized kernel for /batch-embed to compare cost/latency.

leo: I'll keep the reconciliation alert live and post incidents if delta >1% for >30m.

sam: Thanks all — finance will hold off auto-crediting until we confirm root cause. If we need to issue credits we'll use the `runtime_tokens_consumed` ground truth.

anya: Great collaboration — keeping this thread as the single source of truth for the billing->runtime reconciliation. Please @mention when you post dashboard screenshots or PRs.
